stemMd: Choose the revision that correctly links two complete clauses: "The telescope was ready, the clouds blocked the sky."

options.label: B
options.textMd: The telescope was ready, but the clouds blocked the sky.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The telescope was ready the clouds blocked the sky.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The telescope was ready, the clouds still blocked the sky.

explanationMd: Both parts can stand as sentences. A comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" joins them and expresses the contrast between readiness and poor viewing conditions.

distractorRationale.d: A comma alone cannot join these independent clauses.
distractorRationale.c: Without punctuation or a conjunction, the clauses run together.
distractorRationale.a: Although has no following subordinate clause and does not link the statements.
